title: Throughput subsidy and billing margins — scratchpad
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
This is a personal scratchpad for sketching a hybrid pricing approach that blends per-token billing with a throughput/latency subsidy (reserved throughput credit). Goal: preserve simple PLG-friendly per-token signals while giving us levers to control tail latency, amortize GPU costs, and create predictable ARPU for small teams.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline model family for hosted API: 7B/13B-ish general purpose.
- Amortized infra cost (including infra, redis/cache, networking, monitoring, ops) for one inference GPU equivalence: ~$5.00/hr (ballpark; varies by instance, region, occupancy).
- Serving throughput (effective tokens/sec) per GPU (mixed-length workload): 800 tok/s average (7B-ish with batching and KV cache).
- Effective tokens/hour per GPU ~ 2.88M tokens/hr (800 * 3600).
- Cost per 1M tokens (in infra only) ~= $5.00 / 2.88 ≈ $1.74 per 1M tokens.
- Add overhead (support, platform, margin) target: 3x on infra -> target COGS-to-list multiplier = 3x; target price per 1M tokens ≈ $5.20.

But we can massively improve unit economics with caching, batching, and off-peak multiplexing. For bursty, latency-sensitive traffic we need reserved headroom (subsidy).

Key idea: Two-part pricing for hosted API (for small/mid customers):
1) Base subscription (throughput credit) — monthly fee provides guaranteed concurrency/throughput and a pool of "throughput credits" that implicitly buy reserved GPU capacity (short-term bursts from a reserved pool).
2) Per-token consumption above free allotment — dynamic metering at a published per-1M rate, with cheaper tiers if you buy larger monthly credit commitments.

Why this helps:
- Base subs lets us turn many small customers into predictable ARR and absorb some of the variance in traffic (easier capacity planning).
- Credits tied to throughput (e.g., credit = equivalent of X tokens/hr capacity) let us express latency SLOs (guaranteed throughput) rather than raw tokens which are ambiguous for burstiness.
- Allows discounts for customers optimizing for cost (encourages batching/caching).

Design knobs and quick rules-of-thumb:
- Define 1k throughput-credits (TC) = enough credit to sustain 1 token/sec for 1000s? Hmm too confusing. Simpler: define credits as "equivalent GPU-seconds".
  - 1 credit unit (CU) = 1 GPU-second of reserved-equivalent capacity.
  - If 1 GPU delivers 800 tok/s then 1 CU -> 800 tokens. Over a minute (60s) CU provides 48k tokens.
- Example mapping: 1 CU = 800 tokens (instantaneous capacity). For monthly packaging, sell buckets of CU per month.

Back-of-envelop price mapping (rough):
- Infra cost per CU: from earlier, 1 GPU-hour ~3600 CU if 1 CU = 1 GPU-second. Infra cost per GPU-hour = $5 -> per CU = $5 / 3600 ≈ $0.00139.
- If we sell CU at $0.004 each (≈3x margin), then one 1M token equivalent (approx 1250 CU at 800 tok/CU? need consistent mapping). Let's translate carefully:
   - 1 CU = 800 tokens (instant instantaneous, but over time usage drains CU).
   - To deliver 1M tokens at 800 tok/s assumptions naive instantaneous CU consumption = 1M / 800 ≈ 1250 CU (this maps to ~1250 GPU-seconds = ~0.347 hours).
   - Infra cost of 1250 CU = 1250 * $0.00139 ≈ $1.74 (matches earlier tokens-based COGS).
   - If we price 1250 CU at 3x cost -> price ≈ $5.20 per 1M tokens.

Packaging sketches (monthly):
- Solo Starter: $12/month -> includes 250k tokens (~$48 per 1M implicit price) + 2 seats small burst allowance (tiny pool of CU). Overage $10 per 100k. (aimed at experimentation, intentionally low commitment but high overage to encourage upgrade).
- Team Micro: $49/month -> includes 1.5M tokens + 5k CU pool (mapping gives guaranteed concurrency for small teams). Overage $4 per 100k tokens.
- Team Growth: $249/month -> includes 8M tokens + 40k CU pool + 3 seats + priority support. Overage $3 per 100k.
- Scale / SMB Reserved: $1,500/month -> includes 60M tokens + 400k CU + SLA for 99.5 latency SLO and 10x cheaper overage $0.8 per 1M. (Committed reserved capacity equivalently purchased)

Seat vs token tradeoffs:
- For some customers the dominant value is concurrency/latency not raw tokens. Offer seat add-on for developer tooling and workspaces: $20/seat/month includes per-seat small token allocation and admin controls; high-concurrency seats require CU pool.

Experiment ideas to validate quickly (A/B candidates):
- Variant A: larger explicit token packages only (status quo) vs Variant B: small weekly CU credit subscription showing "guaranteed realtime capacity" as marketing message. Measure conversion uplift and retention.
- Offer a temporary CU discount for customers with high batching potential (we can identify by low tokens/session and high tokens/second ratio).
- Try a 14-day trial with 50k CU (enough to sustain ~1k tok/s bursts) to simulate product-led "real-time demo" experience.

Measurement and telemetry we need to instrument: (quick list)
- CU burn rate per customer, spikes, peak concurrent CU consumption, tokens-per-session distribution.
- Cache hit ratio and KV prefix reuse rate (to estimate potential CU savings if they adopt caching).
- Conversion funnel by CU exposure (did customers with CU trial convert at higher rate?).

Risks / open questions:
- Complexity: will CU abstraction confuse buyers? Mitigation: expose two surfaces: simple token bundles for shoppers, CU for teams wanting predictable latency / reserved capacity.
- Accounting accuracy: mapping CU to tokens depends heavily on model family and sequence lengths; need to normalize (we may publish "equivalent tokens at 800 tok/s baseline" and provide a calculator).
- Channel friction: enterprise sales will want explicit reserved GPU capacity and SLAs — our CU should be convertible to reserved instances in Dedicated.

Next small steps (actionable):
- Build a small pricing simulator (spreadsheet + simple script) that can take token/session distributions and simulate CU vs pure-token costs for sample customers. Link to PRIC-412.
- Prototype UI copy: "Guaranteed realtime capacity: start with a small monthly throughput credit for predictable latency" and run through checkout usability test.
- Run cohort analysis on recent 3k free-tier accounts to estimate how many would cross thresholds under CU model.

Notes to self: keep packaging simple visually. Customers want a simple headline: price + included tokens + whether they get "realtime guarantee". The CU abstraction can live behind an "advanced options" toggle for those who want to tune latency/cost tradeoffs.

Random scribbles:
- If we can push COGS under $1/1M via better batching/caching we can offer ~$2.50/1M as a sweet spot between volume and margin (still plausible for mid-2025 hardware improvements).
- Consider an auto-convert feature: when a customer hits >X peak CU consumption for Y days, offer a one-click reserved commit with discount and migration of consumed CU to reserved contract.

End of scratchpad (for now).
